Hi Kimberly,

Thanks for the demo last week. Procurement here at CerebriX is looking to lock a reserved capacity commitment for our inference workloads (initial request: 120 A40-equivalent units over 24 months). One ask has come up in our internal review: we need clarity on how Redwood will handle large GPU price swings over the term.

Specifically: can you provide:
- A matrix showing discount tiers by committed $/mo and by tenure (12/24/36 months) with a GPU-cost protection clause (floor that prevents discounts widening if spot GPU costs spike).
- The approval path and expected lead time for exceptions above a baseline discount.

We want to avoid a rigid clause that leaves us exposed if market prices fall, but also need protection if raw GPU costs rise materially.

Appreciate a quick sketch so we can align with our finance and legal teams.

Best,

Hi Sofia — thanks for the clear ask.

Quick overview: Redwood offers tiered commit discounts that combine a committed spend breakpoint and a term. We can include a GPU-price-protection clause that:
- Defines a market-indexed adjustment trigger (monthly) tied to an industry GPU price index;
- Caps customer downside exposure with a price-floor adjustment that limits discount escalation to a pre-agreed delta;
- Allows for an exec exception path for >15% index moves.

I'm looping in Aditya for the discount matrix and Marissa for the approval path and finance guardrails. We'll turn around a concrete matrix and a proposal for how to approve exceptions.

I'll aim to get a first draft tomorrow.

Kim/Marissa/Sofia — attached is a first-pass pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx (summary below). The matrix is built from our current cost model and a simulated GPU-market index. Notes:

Pricing matrix highlights (summary):
- Commit tiers: $250k/mo, $500k/mo, $1M+/mo (these map to approximate A40-equivalent units).
- Term buckets: 12m (baseline), 24m (preferred), 36m (max discount).
- Baseline discount band for 24m at $500k/mo is 28% off list.
- GPU-price protection clause: if index rises >10% month-over-month, we trigger a review and cap additional customer-facing discount increase to +8% relative to baseline (to avoid full pass-through).
- Exec exception: requests for protection beyond the 8% cap route to finance + head of revenue (target SLA for decision: 72 hours).

Questions for Commercial:
1) Do we want to allow an annual true-up (reconciliation) vs quarterly? Annual reduces churn/ops but exposes both sides to larger variance.
2) If customer requires a hard price floor (no discount widening regardless of index), that is a higher-risk option we should price and reserve approval.

Attachments: pricing_matrix_v1.xlsx (contains scenario tabs and cost assumptions).

—Aditya
Principal, Capacity Economics — Redwood Inference

Thanks Aditya — matrix looks reasonable as a starting point. A few commercial constraints from finance:
- We can accept a quarterly true-up (preferred) rather than annual if the customer insists on a tighter protection cadence, but that increases ops.
- We will only entertain a hard floor (no widening discounts under any market move) as a priced, standalone add-on that requires exec approval.
- For the proposed 8% protective cap, finance will sign off if: (a) the customer commits at minimum $500k/mo for at least 24 months, and (b) we insert a macro-exit clause if index moves cumulative >30% in a rolling 6-month window.

Approval path recommendation:
1) Rep (Kim) secures initial legal redlines and customer sign-off on the basic matrix.
